definitions.explanation: The quality or degree of being strong, whether in physical power, mental fortitude, or competitive ability.
The degree or intensity of something such as wind, flavor, or a feeling.

examples.japanese: チームの{強|つよ}さを{見|み}せた。
{彼女|かのじょ}の{精神的|せいしんてき}な{強|つよ}さには{感心|かんしん}する。
{逆境|ぎゃっきょう}でも{諦|あきら}めない{強|つよ}さがあるからこそ、{彼|かれ}は{成功|せいこう}できた。
examples.english: He was able to succeed precisely because he had the strength not to give up even in adversity.

examples.japanese: {風|かぜ}の{強|つよ}さが{増|ま}してきた。
examples.english: The intensity of the wind has been increasing.

examples.japanese: コーヒーの{強|つよ}さを{調整|ちょうせい}できる。
examples.english: You can adjust the strength of the coffee.

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}の{揺|ゆ}れの{強|つよ}さは{場所|ばしょ}によって{異|こと}なる。
examples.english: The intensity of earthquake shaking varies by location.

notes:
The noun form of the i-adjective {強|つよ}い (strong), formed with the suffix -さ which converts adjectives into nouns expressing degree. This is a highly productive pattern in Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {精神的|せいしんてき}な{強|つよ}さ: mental strength
- {風|かぜ}の{強|つよ}さ: wind strength
- {強|つよ}さを{発揮|はっき}する: to demonstrate strength
- {本当|ほんとう}の{強|つよ}さ: true strength

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {力|ちから}: power, force — a broader term for physical or metaphorical power
- {強度|きょうど}: intensity, strength — technical term used for materials, light, or signals
- {丈夫|じょうぶ}さ: durability, sturdiness — emphasizes resistance to damage or wear
